subject: chemistry
title: Colour Cosmos: Test Tube Tales
welcome_lead: Identify transition metal ions by their characteristic colour changes.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on identification of transition metal aqua ions.
final_note: You've decoded the rainbow of test-tube chemistry.

concepts.def: Reacts with both acid and base.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Adding NaOH gives a coloured hydroxide precipitate. Cu^2+ -> blue Cu(OH)2. Fe^2+ -> green Fe(OH)2 (browns in air to Fe(OH)3).

Fe^3+ -> orange/brown Fe(OH)3. Al^3+ -> white Al(OH)3 (dissolves in excess NaOH as [Al(OH)4]-).

Few drops NH3 -> same hydroxide ppt as NaOH.

Excess NH3: Cu(OH)2 dissolves as deep blue [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]^2+. Most others stay precipitated.

[Cu(H2O)6]^2+ + 4Cl- -> [CuCl4]^2- (yellow). Reversible by dilution with water.

[Co(H2O)6]^2+ (pink) + 4Cl- -> [CoCl4]^2- (blue). Shift seen in 'cobalt chloride' moisture indicator.
